source: Assembled on 2026-10-09 from official and government sources; every entry carries its own source_url and last_verified date. No number is published here that could not be traced to a source: entries whose source was secondary or conflicting carry needs_verification=true and say why in verification_note. A person must re-check this file before it ships to anyone in distress (AGENTS.md safety rule 6).
disclaimer: These lines are free, confidential and staffed by trained people. Manovia is not a crisis service and cannot send help to you.

resources.name: 112 — India emergency number (ERSS)
resources.instructions: One number for police, fire, ambulance and women's safety. The 112 India app can send a panic alert.
resources.description: India's single national emergency number. Call it if you or someone with you is in immediate physical danger.
resources.verification_note: Number confirmed by the C-DAC Emergency Response Support System page and Ministry of Home Affairs reporting; the canonical 112.gov.in site was not reachable from the build sandbox.

resources.name: Tele-MANAS (national mental health helpline)
resources.instructions: Toll free. Alternate toll-free number: 1-800-891-4416. You choose the language when you call.
resources.description: Government of India's free, round-the-clock tele-mental-health service. Trained counsellors listen, and can connect you to a mental health professional, a video consultation or local services.

resources.name: Vandrevala Foundation
resources.instructions: Call or send a WhatsApp message to the same number.
resources.description: A free crisis-intervention and counselling helpline run by a national mental-health non-profit, available by phone and WhatsApp.
resources.verification_note: The foundation's own current page lists +91 9999 666 555; older articles also list 1860-2662-345 and 1800-233-3330, which are not published on the site today.

resources.name: iCall (TISS psychosocial helpline)
resources.instructions: Free telephone and email counselling: icall@tiss.ac.in. Two-way anonymous — they do not ask for your name.
resources.description: A psychosocial helpline run by the Tata Institute of Social Sciences, including support for abuse, violence, gender and sexuality concerns.
resources.verification_note: The number is consistent across iCall's own pages, but the published hours conflict: one page says Mon–Sat 8:00 am–9:00 pm, another says 10:00 am–8:00 pm. Confirm the hours with iCall before shipping.

resources.name: KIRAN (mental health rehabilitation helpline)
resources.instructions: Toll free, launched by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment (DEPwD).
resources.description: A national toll-free first-line counselling and referral helpline for stress, anxiety, depression and suicidal thoughts, with a focus on persons with disabilities.
resources.verification_note: Only secondary sources were reachable from the build sandbox (ThePrint, 2020, and a state National Health Mission helpline PDF). No current ministry page was found. Confirm with MoSJE/DEPwD that the line is still staffed before shipping.

resources.name: AASRA
resources.description: A Mumbai-based crisis-intervention centre for people who are lonely, distressed or suicidal.
resources.verification_note: Listed in a state National Health Mission helpline PDF and in the Find A Helpline directory, but aasra.info itself was not fetched from the build sandbox and third-party listings disagree about hours. Verify by calling before shipping.

resources.name: 911 — emergency services
resources.instructions: Text-to-911 is available in many (not all) US areas.
resources.description: Police, fire and ambulance. Call it if you or someone with you is in immediate danger or needs urgent medical help.

resources.name: 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline
resources.instructions: Free and confidential. You can also call if you are worried about someone else.
resources.description: The US national lifeline for mental-health, suicide and substance-use crises, answered by trained crisis counsellors.

resources.name: Crisis Text Line
resources.instructions: Text HOME to 741741.
resources.description: Free, confidential text-message support from a trained volunteer crisis counsellor.

resources.name: 988 Lifeline — online chat
resources.instructions: A short pre-chat survey connects you to a crisis counsellor.
resources.description: The same 988 Lifeline support by web chat, for when talking out loud is not possible.

resources.name: Veterans Crisis Line
resources.instructions: Dial 988, then press 1. No need to be enrolled in VA benefits or care.
resources.audience: veterans, service members and their families
resources.description: Confidential crisis support from the US Department of Veterans Affairs; many responders are veterans themselves.

resources.name: The Trevor Project (TrevorLifeline)
resources.description: Free, confidential crisis intervention and suicide prevention for LGBTQ+ young people.

resources.name: Veterans Crisis Line — text
resources.audience: veterans, service members and their families
resources.description: The Veterans Crisis Line by text message, free and confidential.

resources.name: The Trevor Project — TrevorText
resources.instructions: Text START to 678-678.
resources.description: Crisis support by text from counsellors trained in LGBTQ+ identities.

resources.name: 999 — emergency services
resources.instructions: 112 also reaches the same services. Free from any phone.
resources.description: Police, ambulance, fire and coastguard. Call it if someone's life is at risk, if they have seriously hurt themselves, or if you need urgent medical help.
resources.verification_note: Confirmed by NHS trust crisis pages (999 for immediate danger, 111 option 2 for urgent mental health). The canonical gov.uk page returned 404 from the build sandbox, so an NHS source is cited instead.

resources.name: Samaritans
resources.instructions: Free from any phone in the UK and Ireland, and the call does not appear on your phone bill.
resources.description: A listening ear for anything that is getting on top of you, including suicidal feelings. You can also email jo@samaritans.org.

resources.name: Shout 85258
resources.instructions: Text the word SHOUT to 85258. Messages do not appear on your phone bill.
resources.description: The UK's free, confidential text support service for anyone struggling to cope.

resources.name: NHS 111, option 2 (urgent mental health)
resources.instructions: Call 111 and select option 2 to reach your local NHS mental health crisis service.
resources.description: NHS urgent mental health help when you are not in immediate physical danger: they can assess you and connect you to a local crisis team.

resources.name: Childline
resources.instructions: Free, and the call does not show up on the phone bill. Online chat is also available.
resources.description: A free, private and confidential service for anyone under 19 in the UK, about anything at all.

resources.name: 000 — Triple Zero
resources.instructions: Free from any phone. 112 also works from a mobile phone. 106 is the text emergency call service for TTY users.
resources.description: Australia's emergency number for life-threatening or time-critical situations: police, fire and ambulance.

resources.name: Lifeline Australia
resources.instructions: Online chat is also available 24/7 at lifeline.org.au.
resources.description: Australia's national crisis support and suicide prevention service, for you or for someone you are worried about.

resources.name: Lifeline Australia — text
resources.instructions: Text 0477 13 11 14; you start with a short anonymous survey.
resources.description: Confidential one-to-one text support with a trained Lifeline crisis supporter.

resources.name: Suicide Call Back Service
resources.instructions: Free nationwide. Video and online counselling are also available.
resources.description: Government-funded counselling for anyone feeling suicidal, worried about someone at risk, or bereaved by suicide.

resources.name: Beyond Blue
resources.description: Counselling and information for anxiety, depression and other mental health concerns.

resources.name: Kids Helpline
resources.instructions: Web chat and email counselling are also available.
resources.description: A free, private counselling service for young people in Australia, about anything.
resources.verification_note: The number and 24/7 availability come from the Australian Government's healthdirect page; kidshelpline.com.au itself was not fetched from the build sandbox.

resources.name: 911 — emergency services
resources.description: Police, fire and ambulance. Call it if you or someone with you is in immediate danger or needs urgent medical help.
resources.verification_note: The FCC's consumer page states that 911 is the official emergency number in the United States and Canada; a Government of Canada page was not reachable from the build sandbox.

resources.name: 9-8-8 Suicide Crisis Helpline
resources.instructions: Free and toll free across every province and territory. Interpreters can be arranged.
resources.description: Canada's national helpline for anyone thinking about suicide or worried about someone else, answered by trained responders.

resources.name: 9-8-8 Suicide Crisis Helpline — text
resources.instructions: Text 9-8-8 from a mobile phone; you are asked whether you want English or French.
resources.description: The same 9-8-8 support by text message, free across Canada.

resources.name: Kids Help Phone
resources.instructions: Professional counsellors, confidential and anonymous, any device.
resources.description: Canada's 24/7 e-mental-health service for young people; a 9-8-8 network partner.

resources.name: Kids Help Phone — text
resources.instructions: Text CONNECT to 686868. Text STOP at any time to end the conversation.
resources.description: Free, confidential text support from a trained volunteer crisis responder.

resources.name: Talk Suicide Canada
resources.instructions: Toll free. Text 45645 between 4 pm and midnight ET.
resources.description: A toll-free line for anyone in Canada with concerns about suicide.
resources.verification_note: Confirmed by the Government of Alberta's health page and Ontario CMHA; talksuicide.ca itself was not fetched from the build sandbox.

resources.name: 112 — international emergency number
resources.instructions: Works from most mobile phones even with no signal on your own network or no SIM.
resources.description: The international standard emergency number. If you do not know your local number, try 112 from a mobile phone.

resources.name: Find A Helpline
resources.description: A vetted directory of crisis and emotional-support helplines in 175+ countries, with phone, text and online chat options.

resources.name: Befrienders Worldwide
resources.description: A global network of emotional-support centres; use the centre finder for a helpline in your country.
